objective: On the unresolved T2-O scalar carrier, test the simplest direct late-XOR valuation law after rank phase has been factored explicitly.
frozen_representation: post-RFG component-type multiplicity parity M2 plus rank mod 3
relative_value: U=+1 if exact V is a win for the current mover, U=0 for draw, U=-1 for loss

affine_xor_candidate.equation: code(U(P)) = b_G,r3 XOR XOR_{component types C with odd multiplicity} g_G(C)
unknowns: one 2-bit value g_G(C) per observed component type
one 2-bit phase offset b_G,r3 for each rank-mod-3 class
affine_xor_candidate.note: Any three distinct GF(2)^2 outcome codes are affine-equivalent, so fixing one injective code removes only coordinate gauge, not a genuine affine solution.

control.purpose: test whether the explicit rank-mod-3 offset is genuinely load-bearing

anti_circularity: Component extractor, parity projection, rank phase and T2 domain are frozen before values are derived.
Exact values supply only the right-hand side of the linear qualification system.
The test does not add new features or patched operands after observing contradictions.
Per-geometry valuation g_G is permitted because the governing objective explicitly allows persistent G.
falsifiers: A zero-coefficient row with nonzero two-bit right-hand side rejects the affine GF(2)^2 valuation in that geometry.
A failure with phase offsets rejects this simplest direct two-bit XOR outcome code even though a larger/nonlinear decoder or another finite algebra may remain possible.
nonclaims: A finite consistent solution does not prove a closed-form component valuation.
A finite consistent solution does not prove standard-7x6 qualification.
This test concerns Q-V only and deliberately ignores the finer Q-A interface.
